selected.sourceTitle: Tonnetz Theory, Classical Harmony, and the Combinatorial Geometry of Abstract Musical Resources
selected.extractionSummary: This arXiv preprint develops a formal mathematical framework connecting musical harmony to combinatorial geometry through the concept of the Tonnetz (tone network). The authors demonstrate that various musical systems — including diatonic triads, diatonic seventh chords, pentatonic scales, and the 12-tone system — each correspond to specific combinatorial configurations (e.g., Fano, Desargues, Cremona-Richmond). A key result is that the Eulerian tonnetz maps to a Daublebsky von Sterneck D222 configuration, and that this same structure describes the relationship between chromatic pitch classes and major triads. The paper also addresses the major/minor triad duality, showing it can be 'broken' by identifying minor triads with hexacycles in the Levi graph of the D222 configuration. The work frames music theory as an instance of abstract combinatorial geometry, offering these structures as explicit resources for composition.

claims.text: The Eulerian tonnetz can be represented by a {12_3} combinatorial configuration of Daublebsky von Sterneck type D222.

citations.label: core result from prior work, recapitulated here
citations.quote: It was shown that the Eulerian tonnetz can be represented by a {12_3} of Daublebsky von Sterneck type D222.

claims.text: The tonnetz for Tristan-genus chords (dominant sevenths and half-diminished sevenths) can be represented by a {12_3} combinatorial configuration of type D228.

citations.label: Tristan-genus tonnetz
citations.quote: We also constructed a tonnetz for Tristan-genus chords (dominant sevenths and half-diminished sevenths) and we showed that this tonnetz can be represented by a {12_3} of type D228.

citations.label: diatonic triads graph
citations.quote: In the case of diatonic triads, we show the existence of a bipartite graph of type {7_3} and girth four that represents the well-known relations between the seven diatonic degrees and their pitch classes.

citations.label: Fano configuration and seventh chords
citations.quote: In the case of diatonic seventh chords, we obtain a Fano configuration {7_3} which gives a complete characterization of the voice-leading relations that hold between such chords.

citations.label: pentatonic tonnetz

citations.label: 12-tone tonnetz
citations.quote: We construct a tonnetz for the 12-tone system based on the Cremona-Richmond configuration {15_3}. Both can be used as a resource for musical compositions.

claims.text: The relationship between the chromatic pitch class set and the major triad set is represented by the same D222 configuration as the Eulerian tonnetz.

citations.label: chromatic–major triad correspondence
citations.quote: We show that the relation between the chromatic pitch class set and the major triad set is also represented by a D222.

claims.text: Minor triads correspond one-to-one with a certain class of hexacycles in the Levi graph of the D222 configuration, allowing the major/minor duality of the traditional tonnetz to be broken.

citations.label: minor triads and hexacycles
citations.quote: The minor triads are in one-to-one correspondence with the members of a certain class of hexacycles in the Levi graph of this configuration. In this way, the characteristic duality between major and minor triads in the tonnetz can be broken.

openQuestions: Can the Desargues {10_3} pentatonic tonnetz be used to generate novel voice-leading rules analogous to those derived from the Fano configuration for diatonic seventh chords?
What are the perceptual or acoustic correlates of navigating paths through the Cremona-Richmond {15_3} 12-tone tonnetz — do certain paths correspond to recognizable harmonic progressions?
Since minor triads are modeled as hexacycles rather than as dual objects to major triads in this framework, what new compositional symmetries or asymmetries does this asymmetric treatment enable?
Are there analogous combinatorial configurations for microtonal or non-Western tuning systems (e.g., 19-TET, 31-TET, maqam scales)?
How does the D228 configuration for Tristan-genus chords relate acoustically to the harmonic series — is the dominant seventh's proximity to just intonation ratios reflected in the geometry?

Can these abstract graph structures be directly sonified or mapped to generative composition algorithms, and if so, what traversal strategies (e.g., Hamiltonian paths, shortest paths) yield musically coherent results?
What is the relationship between the girth-four constraint of the diatonic triad bipartite graph and perceptual properties like harmonic ambiguity or voice-leading efficiency?

selected.sourceTitle: Is ASMR Engineerable? A Signal Processing and User Experience Study
selected.extractionSummary: This preprint investigates whether Autonomous Sensory Meridian Response (ASMR) can be deliberately engineered through controlled acoustic design. The study uses signal processing and a structured user study to map acoustic features to perceived ASMR effects. Key findings suggest that cyclic sound patterns balancing predictability (for relaxation) and variation (for sustained interest) are the most effective triggers. Smoothly spread, energy-dense cyclic patterns were found to be the most reliable inducers of ASMR. The results indicate that relaxation effects accumulate progressively, are spatially invariant, and stable over time.

citations.label: main finding
citations.quote: smoothly spread, energy-dense cyclic patterns most effectively trigger ASMR, suggesting that signal-level engineering of ASMR experiences is achievable

citations.label: spatial invariance finding
citations.quote: relaxing effects accumulate progressively, are independent of spatial orientation, and remain stable across time

citations.label: motivation / gap statement
citations.quote: ASMR effects validated through behavioral studies and neuro-physiological measurements such as electroencephalography (EEG) and related bio-signals, the acoustic mechanisms that trigger it remain poorly understood

openQuestions: What specific frequency ranges or spectral bands are most associated with ASMR induction—can a target spectral profile be specified for composition?
Is there an optimal ratio of predictability to randomness in cyclic patterns that maximizes ASMR while minimizing habituation?
How does the rate of cyclic repetition (tempo/period) interact with ASMR induction—are there privileged tempos or cycle lengths?
Can these engineered cyclic patterns be embedded into conventional musical structures (e.g., ostinatos, loops) without disrupting their ASMR efficacy?
Does spatial independence of ASMR response hold for binaural or ambisonic audio, and does this inform multichannel composition strategies?
What is the relationship between ASMR-inducing acoustic structures and known psychoacoustic phenomena such as the 'chills' (frisson) response to music?
Could progressive accumulation of relaxation effect be exploited compositionally through long-form, slowly evolving cyclic textures (e.g., drone music, generative systems)?
Are there individual or cultural differences in response to engineered ASMR patterns that would affect compositional universality?

selected.sourceTitle: From Napoleon Dynamite to Cyberpunk 2077: How NI shaped Brian McNelis’s story
selected.extractionSummary: Brian McNelis is a music supervisor and producer whose career spans electronic music, film soundtracks, and AAA game scores, with Native Instruments tools serving as a continuous thread throughout. The article describes his workflow for bridging non-technical stakeholders (directors, executives) with composers by using shared sonic vocabulary and rapid sketching tools. The Cyberpunk 2077 project required ~150 exclusive tracks, a four-year timeline, and a production infrastructure built around iterative sound design feedback with contributing artists. His account offers a practitioner's view of how digital production tools changed the economics and logistics of music production from the late 1990s onward. The article is promotional in nature, published by Native Instruments, and contains no peer-reviewed or empirically verified claims.

selected.sourceTitle: Predicting Upcoming Stuttering Events from Three-Second Audio: Stratified Evaluation Reveals Severity-Selective Precursors, and the Model Deploys Fully On-Device
selected.extractionSummary: This paper presents a CNN-based system for predicting stuttering events from 3-second audio clips, trained on the SEP-28k dataset. The model reveals that severe disfluency events (blocks and sound repetitions) carry detectable prosodic precursors in audio, while fillers and word repetitions do not. The system is compact (616K parameters) and deployable on-device with sub-millisecond latency. The finding that clinically severe events concentrate prosodic precursor signal is the most musically/acoustically relevant insight, as it implies that prosodic features in short audio windows carry predictive information about upcoming speech events.

citations.label: prosodic explanation
citations.quote: The aggregate objective converges to a severity-selective predictor because severe events carry prosodic precursors; fillers do not.

claims.text: A 3-second audio window is sufficient to extract prosodic features that predict upcoming speech disfluency events with above-chance accuracy.

citations.label: prediction from 3-second window
citations.quote: We train a 616K-parameter CNN on SEP-28k (Apple, 20,131 three-second clips) to predict whether the next contiguous clip contains any disfluency.

claims.text: Prosodic precursor signals in speech audio are severity-selective: they encode information about upcoming disruptions in temporal and spectral structure, suggesting that prosody carries anticipatory information not uniformly distributed across event types.

citations.label: prosodic precursor specificity
citations.quote: severe events carry prosodic precursors; fillers do not

citations.label: streaming feasibility
citations.quote: A 4 Hz streaming simulation uses 0.54% of the real-time budget.

citations.label: on-device latency
citations.quote: Neural-Engine latency per 3 s window: 0.25 ms (iPhone 17 Pro Max, A19 Pro) to 0.55 ms

openQuestions: What specific prosodic features (pitch trajectory, energy envelope, spectral flux, rhythmic regularity) in a 3-second window carry predictive information about upcoming events? Could these same features serve as compositional triggers or generative parameters?

If severe stuttering events carry prosodic precursors, do analogous anticipatory prosodic structures exist before other acoustically significant speech events — such as expressive peaks, emotional shifts, or sung phrase endings?

Could a 4 Hz streaming audio analysis system be repurposed to track real-time prosodic state in musical performance, enabling adaptive accompaniment or live processing that anticipates phrase boundaries?
The 3-second window aligns with known short-term auditory memory and phrase-perception windows in music cognition. Is this duration coincidentally or causally optimal for prosodic feature extraction?
What is the acoustic/spectral signature of a 'block' precursor vs. a 'sound repetition' precursor? Are these distinguishable in frequency domain, or primarily in temporal envelope and rhythm?

Could severity-selective detection logic (ignoring filler-like events, responding only to structurally significant disruptions) inspire a compositional system that reacts only to 'severe' musical gestures — sudden silences, harmonic blocks — rather than all events equally?

selected.extractionSummary: Qwen3.5-Omni is a large-scale multimodal AI model trained on over 100 million hours of audio-visual content, supporting audio, video, text, and speech modalities. It introduces ARIA, a system for dynamically aligning text and speech tokenization units to improve streaming speech synthesis stability and prosody. The model supports multilingual speech generation across 10 languages with 'human-like emotional nuance.' It demonstrates strong performance on audio and audio-visual benchmarks, surpassing or matching competing frontier models. The report is primarily a technical AI paper, with limited direct relevance to music theory or acoustics, but contains several claims touching on speech, prosody, and audio representation that may interest the Resonant Projects research context.

selected.sourceTitle: Geo2Sound: A Scalable Geo-Aligned Framework for Soundscape Generation from Satellite Imagery
selected.extractionSummary: Geo2Sound is a machine learning framework that generates geographically realistic soundscapes from satellite imagery by combining geospatial attribute modeling, semantic hypothesis expansion, and geo-acoustic alignment. The system addresses the challenge that existing image-to-audio models struggle with top-down satellite views due to their wide-area semantic ambiguity. The authors introduce SatSound-Bench, a benchmark of over 20,000 paired satellite images, text descriptions, and real-world audio recordings collected across more than 10 countries. Geo2Sound achieves a Fréchet Audio Distance (FAD) of 1.765, outperforming the strongest baseline by 50%, with human evaluations confirming gains in realism (26.5%) and semantic alignment. The work frames soundscape generation as a geographically grounded problem, suggesting that acoustic environments have meaningful spatial structure derivable from overhead imagery.

selected.sourceTitle: Building dialogue in electronic music with Kontakt, Monark, and David Mayer
selected.extractionSummary: David Mayer discusses his production process for 'News Flash,' a track built around an Eastern-leaning lead sampled and manipulated in Kontakt. He describes a hybrid workflow combining Kontakt for textural, expressive realism and Monark for analog bass grit. Central to his compositional philosophy is the principle of 'call and response,' which he applies at the level of beats, melodic phrases, and arrangement sections. He also explores the tension between club functionality and symphonic layering, seeking to embed emotional complexity within dance music structures. The article is a promotional interview with Native Instruments and carries no academic or scientific rigor.

selected.sourceTitle: A Multimodal Data Fusion Generative Adversarial Network for Real Time Underwater Sound Speed Field Construction
selected.extractionSummary: This paper presents MDF-RAGAN, a generative adversarial network for reconstructing underwater sound speed profiles (SSPs) without requiring on-site sonar data. It fuses multimodal data sources (including sea surface temperature) with attention mechanisms and residual modules to estimate how sound propagates through ocean layers. The model achieves under 0.3 m/s error and reduces RMSE by ~65.8% compared to a mean profile baseline. While the application is oceanographic, the underlying physics — sound speed variation as a function of depth, temperature, pressure, and salinity — is directly relevant to underwater acoustics and wave propagation science.

selected.sourceTitle: ATRIE: Adaptive Tuning for Robust Inference and Emotion in Persona-Driven Speech Synthesis
selected.extractionSummary: ATRIE is a text-to-speech synthesis framework designed for anime and digital human avatars that separates voice generation into a static timbre component and a dynamic prosody component. It uses a dual-track architecture distilled from a large language model to maintain consistent character identity across varying emotional contexts. The system is evaluated on a benchmark of 50 anime characters and achieves strong performance on speaker verification and cross-modal retrieval tasks. While primarily an engineering paper, it touches on the computational decomposition of voice into timbre and prosody — constructs with deep roots in music theory and acoustics.

selected.sourceTitle: An Ultra-Low Latency, End-to-End Streaming Speech Synthesis Architecture via Block-Wise Generation and Depth-Wise Codec Decoding
selected.extractionSummary: This paper presents a neural text-to-speech architecture optimized for real-time streaming with ultra-low latency, using discrete codec representations instead of continuous acoustic features. It avoids traditional neural vocoders by directly modeling a compressed latent space via residual vector quantization. The system achieves a time-to-first-byte latency of ~49ms, which the authors claim falls below human perception thresholds for interactive use. It also claims improvements in fundamental voicing accuracy and reduction of high-frequency spectral degradation compared to conventional regression-based systems. The architecture is validated on English and Malay, suggesting language-independent applicability.

selected.sourceTitle: Gaussian Process Regression of Steering Vectors With Physics-Aware Deep Composite Kernels for Augmented Listening
selected.extractionSummary: This paper addresses the problem of representing steering vectors — spatial acoustic responses of microphone arrays — continuously over frequency and position, rather than as discrete measurements. The authors propose a Gaussian Process (GP) framework augmented with a physics-aware deep composite kernel that models both directional incoming waves and their scattering effects. This probabilistic approach overcomes the overfitting limitations of purely deterministic deep learning super-resolution methods, especially under sparse measurement conditions. Applied to augmented listening tasks (speech enhancement and binaural rendering), the method achieves oracle-level performance using fewer than one-tenth the number of measurements previously required. The work is evaluated using the SPEAR challenge dataset.

citations.label: Motivation for probabilistic framework

Specifically, we propose a physics-aware composite kernel that models the directional incoming waves and the subsequent scattering effect.

selected.sourceTitle: Multi-Source Position and Direction-of-Arrival Estimation Based on Euclidean Distance Matrices
selected.extractionSummary: This arXiv preprint proposes new algorithms for estimating the positions and directions-of-arrival (DOAs) of multiple sound sources using microphone arrays, based on Euclidean Distance Matrices (EDMs) and their Gram matrices. The core insight is that exploiting EDM properties reduces the dimensionality of the optimization problem compared to steered-response power (SRP) beamforming — from three continuous variables to one per source for position estimation, and to zero for DOA estimation. The methods rely on estimated time-differences of arrival (TDOAs) between microphones and minimize cost functions defined over eigenvalues of Gram matrices. Experimental results with six microphones in noisy and reverberant environments show the EDM-based approach outperforms SRP-based methods in both accuracy and computational speed.

claims.text: Steered-response power (SRP) beamforming for 3D sound source localization requires joint optimization of three continuous variables for position estimation, making it computationally expensive at high accuracy.

citations.label: computational cost of SRP
citations.quote: SRP-based methods require joint optimization of three continuous variables for position estimation or two continuous variables for DOA estimation, which can be computationally expensive when high localization accuracy is desired.

claims.text: Exploiting Euclidean Distance Matrix properties reduces multi-source position estimation to optimizing only one continuous variable per source (distance to a reference microphone), rather than three.

citations.label: dimensionality reduction via EDM
citations.quote: only a single continuous variable per source, representing the distance to a reference microphone, needs to be optimized.

claims.text: The proposed EDM-based DOA estimation method eliminates continuous variable optimization entirely, determining the optimal TDOA candidate set through eigenvalue-based cost minimization on a rank-reduced Gram matrix.

citations.label: zero-variable DOA optimization
citations.quote: The proposed multi-source DOA estimation method eliminates the need for continuous variable optimization. The optimal set of candidate TDOA estimates is determined by minimizing a cost function defined using the eigenvalues of a rank-reduced Gram matrix.

claims.text: In noisy and reverberant acoustic environments, the EDM-based method consistently outperforms SRP-based methods for both position and direction-of-arrival estimation accuracy, as well as run time, across different two-source and six-microphone configurations.

citations.label: experimental comparison
citations.quote: experimental results for different source and microphone configurations with six microphones show that the proposed EDM-based method consistently outperforms the SRP-based method in terms of position and DOA estimation accuracy and run time.

multi-source scenario tested in noisy reverberant environment
